feed.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT

entry.title: Re: Safer sighashes and more granular SIGHASH_NOINPUT
entry.summary:
In the development of Lightning Network protocols, the handling of secret reuse presents multiple avenues through which funds may be at risk. Secret reuse is particularly perilous in Lightning, necessitating caution when implementing transaction signing mechanisms.
Both SIGHASH_NOINPUT and OP_MASK demonstrate vulnerabilities related to key or script reuse, but their security implications differ. With OP_MASK, the associated danger is restricted to scenarios where the same script is reused; if a single key is applied for both non-lightning and lightning outputs, OP_MASK does not introduce additional risk. Nevertheless, such use cases are rare in practical applications, rendering this protection somewhat theoretical rather than providing tangible benefits in everyday Lightning operations.
Current transaction signing code has been designed with generic principles, emphasizing clarity and maintainability. Adjustments could be made to accommodate specific needs, such as those arising from Eltoo protocol examples, where a solitary OP_MASK placed at the beginning of the script simplifies special casing in functions like GetMaskedScript(). Despite discussions around enhancing security with features like OP_MASK, there appears to be minimal security advantage for Lightning implementations specifically.
Overall, the debate centers on finding the right balance between simplicity and security trade-offs, with a shared commitment to keeping implementations as straightforward as possible without unnecessary complication.
